subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Third-Wave Coffee Shops
description: A quick win: understand Third-Wave Coffee Shops.

hook.text: Third-wave coffee shops treat coffee like wine—single-origin, transparently sourced, and carefully prepared.

buildup.text: First wave was mass consumption (Folgers). Second wave was café culture (Starbucks). Third wave is craft quality.

discovery.text: Third-wave shops pay farmers 2–5x the commodity price and display the farm name on every bag.

twist.text: Critics call it elitist—a $7 pour-over excludes most consumers. Access to quality shouldn't require wealth.

climax.text: Despite criticism, third-wave economics prove that consumers will pay more when quality and story are visible.

punchline.text: Know the farmer, taste the difference, pay the real price.

quiz.question: What defines 'third-wave' coffee?
options: Treating coffee like wine—single-origin, transparent, craft-focused

details.summary: Third-wave coffee shops treat coffee as an artisanal product rather than a commodity. They emphasize single-origin beans, transparent sourcing, light roasting, and skilled barista craft. Shops like Blue Bottle, Intelligentsia, and Counter Culture pioneered this movement in the early 2000s.
details.whyItMatters: The third wave transformed consumer expectations and created demand for higher quality at every step of the supply chain, from farm to cup.
takeaways: Third wave treats coffee as artisanal, not commodity
It emphasizes origin, transparency, and brewing precision
Pioneered by roasters like Blue Bottle and Intelligentsia

faq.question: What distinguishes the three waves of coffee?
faq.answer: First wave was mass-market commodity coffee like Folgers. Second wave, led by Starbucks, introduced espresso drinks and coffee culture. Third wave treats coffee like wine: origin matters, beans are traceable, roasting is intentional, and brewing is a craft.

faq.question: Is there a fourth wave of coffee?
faq.answer: Some argue the fourth wave is happening now, characterized by scientific precision in brewing, direct farmer relationships, sustainability focus, and coffee education for consumers. Others see it as a deepening of third wave principles rather than a distinct new movement.
